defaults.permitted_development: A two-storey extension in England has a much narrower permitted development route than a single-storey project. Rear two-storey additions can sometimes fit within Class A, but side or wraparound schemes often need planning permission. Around historic cores and mixed streets, roof form, brick detailing and how the work meets the original house can matter as much as the raw permitted development measurements.

rules.height_rules: No part should exceed the highest part of the existing roof, and the eaves should not be higher than the existing eaves.
rules.depth_rules: A two-storey rear extension should usually project no more than 3m beyond the original rear wall and must not sit within 7m of the boundary opposite that rear wall if it is to stay within permitted development.
rules.boundary_rules: Upper floors intensify overlooking and overbearing concerns. Councils look closely at rear-boundary separation, side-window positions and the effect on neighbouring gardens and habitable rooms. Around historic cores and mixed streets, roof form, brick detailing and how the work meets the original house can matter as much as the raw permitted development measurements.
rules.roof_rules: The roof pitch should, so far as practicable, match the existing house and the extension should stay clearly behind the principal elevation. Bulky side roofs and forward projection are common reasons permission is needed.
rules.materials_rules: External materials should match or closely relate to the existing house so the upper floor does not look like a separate block perched behind or beside the dwelling. Around historic cores and mixed streets, roof form, brick detailing and how the work meets the original house can matter as much as the raw permitted development measurements.

rules.permitted_development: A two-storey extension can still fall within Class A in England, but in parts of this authority Article 4 or heritage controls may narrow that fallback route. Even where rights remain, the rear-only, depth and boundary tests still apply.

rules.height_rules: The same height rules still apply in sensitive streets: no part above the existing roof and no eaves above the existing eaves line.
rules.depth_rules: A two-storey rear extension should usually project no more than 3m beyond the original rear wall if it is to stay within PD. Once depth, width or side projection increases beyond that, permission is normally needed.
rules.boundary_rules: In tighter or heritage-sensitive streets, upper-floor overlooking and dominance are often judged even more carefully, so rear separation and window positions matter early.
rules.roof_rules: The roof pitch should, so far as practicable, match the existing house and the extension should stay clearly behind the principal elevation. Bulky side roofs and forward projection are common reasons permission is needed.
rules.materials_rules: Close material matching matters even more in heritage-sensitive settings so the upper floor stays visually tied to the existing house.

restrictions.conservation_area: Extensions in a conservation area often need a tighter design and siting assessment, especially on visible elevations or where the scheme would alter roof form, frontage or the rhythm of the street.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on standard householder permitted development rights for a listed building. Listed building consent is usually required for works affecting character, and planning permission may also be needed.
restrictions.article4_notes: Article 4 directions apply in parts of this authority and can remove the usual householder fallback route, so confirm the property's designation before treating the extension as permitted development.

rules.permitted_development: England only allows a limited two-storey PD route under Class A. In practice it is mainly rear extensions that can sometimes qualify, while side and wraparound upper-floor schemes usually need permission.

rules.height_rules: Keep the upper floor below the existing roof height and do not raise the eaves above the existing eaves line.
rules.depth_rules: A two-storey rear extension should usually project no more than 3m beyond the original rear wall if it is to stay within PD. Once depth, width or side projection increases beyond that, permission is normally needed.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary impact is usually the decisive issue with two-storey work. Rear gardens need enough separation, and side-facing upper windows can quickly create overlooking problems.
rules.roof_rules: The roof pitch should, so far as practicable, match the existing house and the extension should stay clearly behind the principal elevation. Bulky side roofs and forward projection are common reasons permission is needed.
rules.materials_rules: Match wall, roof and window finishes closely to the existing house so the upper floor reads as part of the original building rather than a stacked add-on.
